changes: Fixed the R button in wild battles letting you throw a Poké Ball you didn't have, which happened when continuing a save from before 2.1.7 without any Poké Balls.
Website: the damage calculator is rebuilt on Smogon's calculator with Gen 9 battle rules, and shows how each Pokémon imported from your save matches up against the trainer's.
Rayquaza, Kyogre, Groudon, Lugia, Ho-Oh and Deoxys now come back until you catch them. Knocking one out no longer loses it for good.
The Weather Institute keeps finding Kyogre's or Groudon's cave until you have caught both.
Mirage Island now only offers legendaries you can't find anywhere else, so it no longer repeats Pokémon that live elsewhere in Hoenn.
Mirage Island names alternate forms such as Galarian Articuno or Ice Rider Calyrex before the battle, instead of announcing a second "Articuno".

Added the Mirage Altar at the top of Mirage Island. It calls back a Cosmog, Poipole, Kubfu or Type: Null you've caught, so you can get the second one needed for Cosmoem, Naganadel, both Urshifu and Silvally.
After you become Champion, the Bean Shop also sells the Rusted Sword and Rusted Shield.
The Items pocket now holds 165 items and the Key Items pocket 100, up from 150 and 30.
The time you set with the Pocket Watch now lasts through doors and saves until you pick its new Real Time option. Berries and daily events still follow the real clock.
Garchompite Z is now in Ever Grande City instead of on Route 113.
Nuzlocke mode: Mirage Tower now counts as its own area for first encounters, separate from Route 111.
Fixed the Trick House quiz: every question now has matching answers, and the question text is corrected.
Fixed the colours of the Gym Leader and Elite Four sprites in the overworld.
Website: the map shows the Lavaridge Gym B1F trainers and the Lavaridge Town Egg gift.
Website: the damage calculator has its own entry for every Pokémon form and now lists Garchompite Z and the other new Mega Stones.
Website: a trainer's Pokémon opened from the map shows their whole team in the calculator, and trainer moves, abilities and items use their in-game names.
Fainted Pokémon in Nuzlocke mode now stay fainted. Pokémon Centers, the PC, the Day Care and Revives can't bring them back.
Basculin evolves after taking any recoil damage.
Evolving or hatching a Mirage Island legendary no longer uses up another one.
Made the early Gym Leaders easier and the later Gym Leaders and Elite Four harder.
Sleeping trainer Pokémon use Sleep Talk instead of wasting the turn.
Trainers no longer switch out a Yawned Pokémon holding a Chesto or Lum Berry.
Website: the Pokédex lists every evolution condition, and gifts say how to get them.
Website: the map shows Game Corner prizes and the shops trainers open once beaten.
Website: the damage calculator loads Mega Stone holders in their Mega form.
Added the DexNav in Standard mode. It comes with the Pokédex and lets you search for the Pokémon in an area. Chaining raises the odds of Egg Moves, Hidden Abilities, perfect IVs and shinies.
Every Pokémon and every form can now be caught, so you can complete a living dex of all forms.
Wild Pokémon with several looks, like Vivillon, Flabébé and Minior, now appear in any of them, favouring forms you don't have yet.
Mirage Island now has legendary forms like Galarian Articuno, Black and White Kyurem and Dada Zarude. Each can be caught once.
Mirage Island now holds the Gracidea, Reveal Glass, DNA Splicers and other form-changing key items.
The Bean Shop now sells every Sweet and Nectar. After you become Champion it also sells the Plates, Memories, Drives, Masks and Origin items.
A Peat Block evolves Ursaring into Ursaluna at night and into Bloodmoon Ursaluna at any other time.
Pick your starter's nature in the Birch Case, then check its stats before you leave.
SELECT can now hold up to five key items. With more than one registered, it opens a quick list.
You have the Running Shoes from your very first step.
Fishing always gets a bite, and a hooked Pokémon never gets away.
Traded Pokémon always obey you up to your level cap.
The randomizer options have clearer names, and each preset describes what it changes. Birch's randomizer question now starts on No.
Fixed a freeze in Victory Road when a trainer spotted you after a battle.
Fixed sprites flashing bright for a frame during fades in the rain.
Characters in the overworld only show a shadow while jumping, as in the original Emerald. This leaves more room for sprites in busy areas.
Fixed text from earlier lines of Birch's intro showing under later ones.
Fixed the Picnic Basket message still calling it the Poké Vial.
The map on this website remembers where you were when you come back to it. Pokémon and item pages now show the items wild Pokémon hold.
HM moves can be replaced like any other move. No more trip to the Move Deleter, and HMs still work straight from the Bag.
Randomizing wild Pokémon no longer changes Wally's Ralts. His catch follows the trainer options now, and it is the line he brings to Mauville.
Seed codes made in 2.1.3 Beta no longer load, because Wally's Pokémon changed. Make and share a new code.
Randomized starters can now be any Pokémon. One that knows no damaging move at level 5, such as Magikarp or Abra, is handed Tackle so the first battle is still winnable.
Added a Legendaries choice to the Starters option: every ball in the Birch Case holds a legendary, mythical or Ultra Beast, each a different type.
Seed codes made in 2.1.2 Beta no longer load, because randomized starters changed. Make and share a new code.

Added a built-in randomizer. After the mode question, Birch offers to randomize starters, wild Pokémon, trainers, abilities, moves and items. Pick the Randomlocke, Full or Chaos preset or set each option yourself.
Every randomized game has a seed code, shown on your Trainer Card. Share it so friends can play exactly the same game, for example in a Soul Link.
Randomizing is chosen once for a new game and can't be changed later. Existing saves stay unrandomized, and this website always shows the normal game.
Hid the Tera Type on the Pokémon summary screen.
New games start with Fast text speed.
Fixed the credits, the Petalburg Pokémon Center and the Game Corner doll always treating your starter as Treecko in new games.
Turned EVs off entirely in Nuzlocke mode: your Pokémon gain none and ignore any they already have, and enemy trainers have none. Standard mode keeps EVs.
Removed level caps from Standard mode. Standard players get a new Level Limiter key item from Mom to switch the caps back on at any time. The Candy Jar still stops at your badge level in both modes.
Smoothed Standard mode trainer levels: trainers now rise gradually from the previous level cap up to each gym leader, who sits exactly on the cap. Nuzlocke levels are unchanged.
Rebuilt every rematch as the trainer's original team, 5 levels higher each time.
Strengthened the teams of Sawyer, Shelby and Lung to match nearby trainers.
Use a Poké Ball on a party Pokémon to change the ball it's in. The old ball goes back into your Bag.
Using an HM from the Bag now needs a Pokémon in your party that can learn it. It still doesn't have to know the move, so a Charizard can Fly but not Surf.
Added a Mode row to the trainer card showing Nuzlocke or Standard, and tidied the card's rows.
Fixed a crash when running through Route 120 in the rain.
Fixed the move category icon staying on screen during Wally's catching tutorial.
Fixed black pixels on the Trainer School windows after viewing a Pokémon's summary.
The Trainers page on this website now shows both Nuzlocke and Standard levels.
Expanded the PC from 14 to 41 boxes — 1,230 places to keep Pokémon, enough for the entire Pokédex.
Changed the save format to fit those boxes. Convert your existing save with the Save Converter on this website before you play; the game will not save over an unconverted save.
Fixed the Egg Move Tutor in Verdanturf: it now lists your Pokémon's Egg Moves and takes a Pearl only after a move is learned.
Only catching a pre-Elite Four legendary uses up your pick; knocked-out or fled legendaries return when you re-enter the area.
After becoming Champion, every uncaught pre-Elite Four legendary returns and stays until caught.
Added Regirock, Regice and Registeel to the pre-Elite Four legendaries.
Removed the extra level 50 Latios/Latias encounter from the Southern Island sign.
Every HM in the bag now appears in the party menu wherever it can be used, which fixes the Registeel door.
Fixed remaining out-of-sprite crashes in grass, rain and other busy overworld scenes.
Restored modern HMs for Surf and Fly: having HM03 or HM02 in the bag is enough, as in 1.0.1.
Made Battle Style default to Set, locked to Set in Nuzlocke mode and switchable in Options in Standard mode.
Catching Mew now uses up the pre-Elite Four legendary pick, and legendaries no longer respawn after Champion rematches.
Zapdos now disappears immediately after its battle.
Gave each Granite Cave item ball its own pickup flag so Steelixite and Sablenite can no longer be missed.
Re-enabled the developer menu: hold Select and press Start in the overworld.
Prevented rare black-screen crashes while running through grass in areas with many on-screen effects.
Awarded the National Pokédex alongside the regular Pokédex and upgraded existing saves automatically.
Restored the reusable Candy Jar so it instantly raises a Pokémon to the current badge-based level cap.
Restored the 1.0.1 level-cap rules for battle experience, Rare Candies, and daycare growth.
Fixed event tickets so all four special-island ferry destinations unlock for new and existing saves.
Corrected Pokémon types shown throughout the documentation.
Increased the base Shiny rate from 1 in 8,192 to 1 in 512.
Upgraded the game engine to pokeemerald-expansion 1.16.3 and enabled follower Pokémon.
Made every regular Pokémon and regional form obtainable, with remaining special cases added to the Bean Shop.
Added a postgame Legendary Lottery Island and dozens of Mega Stones to discover across Hoenn.
Reworked all eight Trick House puzzles with 32 region-themed Elite Four cameos, matching sprites, music, and dialogue.
Added new Ace Trainer boss battles and postgame challengers around Hoenn.
Fixed key progression issues involving starters, time-based evolutions, and Nuzlocke catches.
Published the first official release of Pokémon Black Pearl Emerald.
Introduced a reworked Emerald adventure with custom trainer teams, sprites, dialogue, maps, and music.
Added expanded Pokémon content and modern battle mechanics through pokeemerald-expansion 1.8.6.
Added the Bean Shop, Lilycove event-ticket ferry, and expanded legendary encounters.
Improved egg and daycare behavior and polished graphics throughout the game.
